text.arabic_uthmani: وَلَقَدْ جَآءَهُم مِّنَ ٱلْأَنۢبَآءِ مَا فِيهِ مُزْدَجَرٌ

words.gloss_range: opening connector that resumes the previous indictment while launching a certified proof-claim
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) opens as a linked resumption: the new claim about arriving deterrent reports stays attached to the denial and desire-following already named. It also carries the previous settled principle into this proof case. Its oath coloring is narrowed, because no oath noun follows; the live payoff is that discourse linkage and certification arrive together.

topics.headline: linked resumption into emphatic claim
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah is both connected to the prior indictment and freshly launched as a certified claim.
topics.reason: The particle can coordinate or resume, and the following confirmation cluster makes resumption into a proof-claim the strongest local function; oath force is retained only as reinforcement.

topics.headline: boundary carries principle into proof-instance
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the settled principle of the previous ayah feeding directly into the evidentiary case of this ayah.
topics.reason: The boundary row makes the new statement an instance of the preceding principle rather than a detached report.

words.gloss_range: asseverative particle fused to the certainty marker, certifying the whole completed arrival claim
words.prose: {{ar:لَ}} ({{tr:la}}) compresses oath-related and direct assertion force into the clause opening. Bound to the next certainty marker, it certifies the arrival and the embedded deterrence as one claim aimed at resistant hearers.

topics.headline: bound asseveration scopes over the whole claim
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the whole report-arrival claim is certified for an audience already marked by denial.
topics.reason: The prefixed particle is attached to the following certainty marker before the perfect verb, and the local discourse supplies resistant recipients through the later object suffix.

words.gloss_range: certainty particle before a perfect verb, making the arrival accomplished and verified
words.prose: {{ar:قَدْ}} ({{tr:qad}}) is anchored to the perfect verb that follows, so its range narrows to completed verification. The reports are not pending or merely possible; their arrival is already established evidence.

topics.headline: certainty over a completed arrival
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the reports had already reached them before their resistance is assessed.
topics.reason: The particle immediately precedes a perfect verb, selecting completed verification rather than proximity or reduction readings.

words.gloss_range: completed arrival reaching a specified resistant audience; informational delivery with accountability force
words.root_gloss_range: arrival, coming, reaching, presentation, or befalling; here narrowed to completed delivery of consequential reports to recipients
words.prose: {{ar:جَآءَهُمْ}} ({{tr:jāʾahum}}) makes the audience grammatically affected before the report-source is named. The suffix resumes the deniers already in view, while the perfect form under certification treats the delivery as complete. The verb-first launch lets the arrival event land before the content is specified. The root image is arrival toward a destination, narrowed here to informational reaching with accountability force; the warning-arrival pattern returns later (54:41). The hamza catch makes the arrival word land sharply before the suffix.

topics.headline: object suffix makes the deniers reached recipients
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the reports did not merely exist; they reached the very group whose denial was just described.
topics.reason: The attached object suffix is syntactically forced as the verb object and contextually resumes the prior third-person plural actors.

topics.headline: perfect verb gives completed evidentiary delivery
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that access to the deterrent reports is already a completed fact, not an offer still in progress.
topics.reason: The perfect verb after the certainty particle fixes the event as achieved before the clause characterizes what the reports contain.

topics.headline: verb launches before the subject specification
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the verb-first launch: the event of arrival is heard before the content that came is specified.
topics.reason: The later relative pronoun is licensed as subject or specification while the verb remains default masculine singular in verb-first order.

topics.headline: arrival image becomes delivered evidence
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the reports as incoming evidence that arrives upon recipients rather than as static background information.
topics.reason: The root allows broader coming and befalling images, but the governed report-source phrase narrows the local reading to informational delivery with event-like accountability force.

topics.headline: arrival belongs to a warning-delivery pattern
topics.reader_payoff: The reader recognizes this arrival as a programmatic warning-delivery pattern that later narratives instantiate (54:41).
topics.reason: The rows give concrete parallels for delivered evidence and a same-surah warning arrival, so the local verb can carry that pattern without changing its parse.

topics.headline: hamza gives the arrival word an audible catch
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can hear the arrival word land sharply before the recipient suffix is named.
topics.reason: The phonetic row has a small but concrete payoff: the hamza catch in the surface form reinforces the verb’s abrupt arrival before the suffix.

words.gloss_range: source, partitive, and explanatory hinge introducing the report-domain from which the arrived content is drawn
words.prose: {{ar:مِنَ}} ({{tr:mina}}) keeps the verb-object phrase from closing too soon and turns the clause toward the report-domain. Source, partitive, and explanatory force work together: what came is drawn from and specified by the known body of reports, not equated with the whole archive. Its nasal ending also audibly fastens the preposition to the report noun it governs.

topics.headline: source and partitive force remain together
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the deterrent material is drawn from a larger report-domain while still coming from that domain as source.
topics.reason: The preposition governs the following report noun as a source/partitive complement to the arrival verb; explanatory specification remains compatible with that extraction force.

topics.headline: sound fastens preposition to report noun
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can hear the small function word bind into the report noun it governs.
topics.reason: The phonetic note has limited but real payoff because it matches the syntactic dependency between preposition and complement.

words.gloss_range: the known body of consequential reports, governed as the source-domain from which deterrent content has come
words.root_gloss_range: consequential news, report, notification, making-known, and prophetic report-bearing pressure; here selected as report-content rather than act or bearer
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلْأَنۢبَآءِ}} ({{tr:al-anbāʾi}}) is a definite plural report-corpus, not generic information. Governed by the source preposition, it supplies the domain from which the arrived material is drawn. Its root field gives the reports consequence: they are news capable of changing the recipient's state, with prophetic and elevated-report pressure retained as authority while the local noun remains report-content. The later pronoun can return to this report body, so the reports themselves can be the container of deterrence; the same report thread joins warning-delivery scenes including 54:41. The hamza gives the noun an audible break where the evidence-source is named.

topics.headline: definite plural names a known report body
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the reports are treated as an identifiable body of warning evidence, not vague information.
topics.reason: The definite plural form and source phrase present a known corpus from which the deterrent material is drawn.

topics.headline: genitive complement keeps reports as source-domain
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the reports are not the main subject; they are the governed source-domain after the recipients have been foregrounded.
topics.reason: The noun is genitive under the preceding preposition, keeping the later relative content available as what came.

topics.headline: report means consequential news, not neutral data
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels why reports can contain deterrence: this report-word names weighty news that demands response.
topics.reason: V4 evidence is missing for this root, but the lexical rows remain coherent and are supported by local deterrence content.

topics.headline: prophetic and elevated-source pressure around reports
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices an authority pressure around the reports: they belong to a field tied to prophetic disclosure, while the local sense stays report-content.
topics.reason: The derivational and prophetic-bearer rows carry real semantic pressure, but local grammar selects the abstract plural reports rather than a prophet title or independent elevation sense.

topics.headline: reports can be the container of deterrence
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the reports themselves can function as the container and medium of the corrective force named at the end.
topics.reason: The later resumptive pronoun may return to the report noun or to the relative content, so the reports remain a licensed container for deterrence.

topics.headline: report noun joins delivered-warning pattern
topics.reader_payoff: The reader recognizes the report noun as part of a recurring warning-report delivery pattern, including the later warning-arrival scene (54:41).
topics.reason: The rows cite co-occurrence and warning-report parallels, so the local noun preserves that formulaic role without changing its governed case.

topics.headline: hamza marks the report noun acoustically
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can hear the report-root interrupt the phrase at the point where the evidence-source is named.
topics.reason: The orthographic and phonetic rows add a small surface payoff that does not alter the lexical sense.

words.gloss_range: relative/specifying pronoun that defines the arrived report-material by the deterrence contained in it
words.prose: {{ar:مَا}} ({{tr:mā}}) pivots from the source-domain into the inner content clause. The thing that came is identified by what it contains, while subject versus appositional force remains locally possible. The reports are therefore defined functionally by deterrence, not merely named as information.

topics.headline: relative pronoun defines content by contained deterrence
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah moves from report-source to the specific content whose value is deterrence.
topics.reason: The relative construction is syntactically forced by the following locative clause, and it makes the deterrent-containing property identify the referent.

topics.headline: subject or appositional specification remains open
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a compact ambiguity: the pronoun can be what came or a specification of the reports, but either route leads to the same deterrent content.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence licenses the pronoun as subject or specification of the arrival clause, while apposition remains a local parsing option rather than a separate meaning.

words.gloss_range: fronted locative predicate, in it, making deterrence internal to the specified report-content or reports
words.prose: {{ar:فِيهِ}} ({{tr:fīhi}}) makes containment the path into the final claim. The suffix can resume the specified content or the reports themselves, so deterrence is inside the message-domain, not attached afterward from outside. By fronting the locative, the clause establishes the container before naming what is found there. The light suffix also becomes an audible hinge into the heavier final deterrent noun.

topics.headline: suffix can resume content or reports
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices layered containment: the deterrent can be inside the specified content and inside the reports as a textual domain.
topics.reason: The resumptive pronoun is syntactically forced and may point to the relative content or report noun, so the ambiguity strengthens the containment relation.

topics.headline: fronted locative makes containment the clause frame
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the clause first says in-it before naming deterrence, making embeddedness the organizing claim.
topics.reason: The prepositional phrase is the fronted locative predicate for the delayed nominative deterrent noun, creating a compact nominal clause.

topics.headline: deterrence is internal rather than external
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the reports carry their own deterrent force; the rebuke is not merely outside commentary added later.
topics.reason: The preposition selects interior containment and the nominal architecture presents deterrence as a standing property within the report-content.

topics.headline: light pronoun releases into the heavy deterrent noun
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can hear the locative hinge release into the heavier final word.
topics.reason: The phonetic row contributes a small surface payoff aligned with the syntactic move from container to contained deterrent.

words.gloss_range: an indefinite embedded deterrent, means, or site of being checked and redirected by the reports
words.root_gloss_range: rebuking, checking, forbidding, driving back by voice, self-restraint, and omen-reading by interpreted movement; local sense selects deterrent corrective force, with augury only as sign-reading pressure
words.prose: {{ar:مُزْدَجَرٌ}} ({{tr:muzdajarun}}) is the ayah's landing word: an indefinite delayed nominative that newly asserts real deterrent force inside the reports. Its passive-locative shape lets the reports be both means and site of deterrence, while the root image supplies rebuke, being driven back, and self-restraint rather than mere advice. Augury pressure is narrowed to sign-reading texture. The marked canonical surface preserves derived-form pressure and a harsh cluster, while the final word also answers prior desire as the counter-force tested by the next warning statement. The same root returns when Noah is driven away (54:9), reversing the intended target of deterrence, and also names the single resurrection shout (37:19; 79:13).

topics.headline: indefinite delayed noun newly asserts deterrence
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah closes by newly asserting deterrence as the interpretive takeaway of the whole report clause.
topics.reason: The noun is indefinite, nominative, delayed after the fronted locative, and placed at verse closure, so it supplies the new information and final weight.

topics.headline: passive-locative role makes reports tool and territory
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that deterrence is both a means by which one is checked and a place where that checking is found inside the reports.
topics.reason: Local grammar places the noun after a locative predicate, while the passive/locative analysis lets the reports function as both means and site.

topics.headline: root image turns reports into redirective force
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels deterrence as forceful redirection and possible self-restraint, not as a flat label for warning.
topics.reason: V4 supports the rebuking/checking branch, and the Form VIII passive-locative shape gives the local deterrence affected, inward-facing force.

topics.headline: omen-reading branch adds sign-reading texture
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the reports are not only rebukes to heed but signs whose trajectory must be read.
topics.reason: The augury branch is real in V4, but the local form and clause select deterrent rebuke; omen-reading survives only as sign-reading pressure around consequential reports.

topics.headline: unique Form VIII noun keeps derivational pressure visible
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that deterrence is carried by a marked form whose rougher canonical surface preserves internalized Form VIII pressure.
topics.reason: The variant rows clarify the canonical form by contrast, but they do not replace it; the local payoff is the canonical passive-locative shape and its visible derived-form pressure.

topics.headline: root returns as reversal and cosmic shout
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the root as a thread: deterrence offered to hearers returns when Noah is driven away (54:9), and the root also names decisive cosmic rupture (37:19; 79:13).
topics.reason: The rows give concrete references, so the echo can be retained as an inter-ayah and cross-surah resonance without governing the local parse.

topics.headline: cluster makes deterrence sound abrupt
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can hear the compact consonantal pressure matching the driving-back force of the root.
topics.reason: The sound rows add a concrete recitational payoff, and the qiraat row shows that smoother assimilation would reduce the canonical form’s roughness while preserving sense.

topics.headline: deterrent force counters prior desire and anticipates warnings
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the final word as the counter-force to prior desire and as the deterrence whose effectiveness the next warning statement tests.
topics.reason: The boundary rows tie the closing noun backward to desire-following and forward to the next ayah, making deterrence a structural counter-pressure rather than a generic moral label.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The construction joins arrival, reports, containment, and muzdajar in 54:4.
baseline_models.mechanism: A useful report is brought into the audience's presence and carries a voice-like check; the news is action-bearing rather than merely descriptive.

activation_trace.role: Bringing and presenting something makes the reports an arrival into the hearers' field.
A consequential delivered report supplies the informational carrier.
A voiced rebuke that stops or repels supplies the carrier's intended braking function.

changed_reading.before: Some news reached them and included a warning.
changed_reading.after: The arriving reports are carriers whose contents exert a stopping or turning force.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: Ja'ahum and min al-anba place two movement-capable roots around the reports in 54:4.
baseline_models.mechanism: The doubled movement image makes transmission salient: reports cross from elsewhere into the audience's present, where their transit should terminate in restraint.

activation_trace.role: Coming and occurring marks the report's realized arrival.
Movement from one place to another makes news a mobile transmission rather than a static archive.
Repelling restraint is the functional destination of that movement.

changed_reading.before: News is static information available to the audience.
changed_reading.after: The verse foregrounds a completed transit: consequential reports have crossed into reach, so distance cannot explain the missing response.

context_deltas.mechanism: Visible evidence is met by bodily turning and desire-led following; muzdajar therefore names a stopping capacity inside the reports, not an automatic effect on every receiver.

activation_trace.role: The branch supplies the report's available but resistible stopping force.
A visible mark makes the evidence inspectable before rejection.
Turning one's side away converts nonresponse into an embodied evasion mechanism.
The inclination of desire supplies the competing force that overrides restraint.
Fixity and settlement give the conflict an eventual endpoint beyond immediate refusal.

structural_cues: 54:2-3 place seeing before turning aside and desire-led denial, immediately before 54:4 declares that reports arrived.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies a seen sign, bodily evasion, desire, and eventual settlement; I infer a reception loop that blocks an available brake. Alternatively, q-r-r may mark truth's final settlement without describing the rejecters' state.

changed_reading.before: If the reports contain deterrence, they should necessarily deter.
changed_reading.after: The reports contain a real affordance for restraint, while the preceding reception sequence explains how hearers can actively defeat its effect.

context_deltas.mechanism: The following wisdom, arrival-at-goal, sufficiency, and warning roots sharpen muzdajar into a complete corrective communication whose failure lies in uptake rather than defective delivery.

activation_trace.role: Stopping and repelling supplies the corrective action to be explained.
Prevention and return for reform recast restraint as correction rather than mere intimidation.
Reaching the endpoint marks the corrective communication as fully arrived.
Sufficiency, under explicit negation, separates complete warning material from benefit actually obtained.
Warning that awakens caution names the intended reception of the corrective check.

structural_cues: 54:5 directly follows the indefinite muzdajar with mature wisdom and a negated statement about warnings availing.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies adjacent corrective, completion, sufficiency, and warning images; I treat the adjacency as a functional gloss on 54:4, not as a claim of strict apposition. A live alternative is that 54:5 begins an independent evaluation.

changed_reading.before: Muzdajar is primarily a threat embedded in old reports.
changed_reading.after: Muzdajar is mature corrective wisdom that has fully reached its audience, even though complete delivery does not guarantee benefit.

context_deltas.mechanism: The packet's split mapping of the later call spans speech that inclines and a forceful shove; followed by rapid approach, it activates a spectrum from the report's inward verbal brake to an outward summons that moves bodies.

activation_trace.role: A voice that checks or drives supplies the initial auditory force.
Calling and inclining by speech supplies the later summons on the same auditory continuum.
The non-dominant mapped image of a forceful push makes the summons' coercive edge visible.
Rapid approach supplies bodily motion as the realized result of the later call.

structural_cues: 54:6-8 moves from the caller's summons to sustained, rapid movement toward that caller.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies vocal restraint, a split-mapped call, and rushing response; I supply the escalation arrow from a missed inner check to an outwardly compelling summons. The live alternative is an auditory parallel with no causal escalation.

changed_reading.before: The deterrent is only admonitory speech in the reports.
changed_reading.after: The deterrent begins a voice-force continuum: a check that could redirect inwardly is later mirrored by a summons that redirects bodies.

context_deltas.mechanism: The report about Noah repeats z-j-r after denial and an insanity accusation, but the rebuking force now lands on the messenger; the reports thus contain a social reversal of the very restraint they offer.

activation_trace.role: Consequential report provides the container in which the later Noah scene is read.
Rebuking restraint initially points from the reports toward their hearers.
Attributing falsehood supplies the social act that rejects the report and its bearer.
Covering the intellect with madness supplies the accusation used to disable the messenger's credibility.
The repeated rebuke now targets and drives the messenger, reversing the force's social direction.

structural_cues: 54:9 repeats the focus root z-j-r in a passive verbal form immediately after doubled denial and the madness accusation.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the exact root recurrence and reversed participant structure; I infer that this reversal is part of what the reports contain. Alternatively, 54:9 may only exemplify hostile suppression without revising muzdajar's direction.

changed_reading.before: The reports direct rebuke from warning toward the warned.
changed_reading.after: The reports also expose how the warned can recoil against warning and redirect rebuke onto its bearer.

context_deltas.mechanism: The Noah report unfolds a chain from overpowering through vindication, opening, convergence, measured determination, and recompense; its deterrent is therefore a causal precedent rather than an isolated threat.

activation_trace.role: A consequential report carries the ordered precedent.
Deterrence is the prospective work performed by the precedent.
Overpowering force supplies the crisis that initiates the consequence chain.
Vindication of the wronged supplies the reversal sought from the crisis.
Opening what was closed initiates the material execution of the reversal.
Two opposed flows meeting supplies coordinated convergence rather than random disaster.
Measured planning assigns the convergence an ordered endpoint.
Reciprocal recompense closes the chain by matching consequence to prior action.

structural_cues: 54:9-14 orders rebuke, complaint, opening, convergence, carriage, and recompense as successive events.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the ordered transitions; I infer that their causal intelligibility is the report's deterrent arrow from rejection to consequence. A live alternative is that the sequence demonstrates power without inviting causal projection.

changed_reading.before: The reports warn by stating that punishment occurred.
changed_reading.after: The reports warn by exposing a reproducible consequence structure: suppression reaches crisis, crisis receives vindication, and an ordered response answers prior action.

context_deltas.mechanism: Construction, fastening, a deliberately retained sign, reminder, ease, and recitation form a transmission architecture: the deterrent in reports is engineered to survive, remain visible, and be recoverable in speech.

activation_trace.role: The delivered consequential report is the content that must be carried across time.
Corrective restraint is the function preserved by the transmission architecture.
A broad board used for building or writing couples material carriage with inscription.
Fasteners that bind ship boards supply durable assembly for the carrier.
Leaving an effect behind converts survival into a persistent trace.
A visible mark makes the retained trace publicly legible.
A reminder supplies the trace's intended mnemonic activation.
Opening into ease makes retrieval of the preserved warning accessible.
Reading and recitation provide the renewable vocal carrier.
Recall after forgetting turns accessible recitation into renewed restraint.

structural_cues: 54:13-17 moves from a constructed carrier through a retained sign to repeated recollection language and recitation.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies ship construction, a retained sign, and easy recitation; I infer one cross-media transmission architecture. Alternatively, the vessel-sign and the recited reminder may be adjacent but independent carriers.

changed_reading.before: The reports arrive mainly as transient oral information.
changed_reading.after: The reports' deterrent is preserved across material trace, visible sign, memory, and repeatable recitation, making it durable without making uptake compulsory.

Render it only as a context-triggered material analogy, never as the lexical translation of ja'a.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The j-y-ʾ root at 54:4 governs the arrival of the reports that contain muzdajar.

activation_trace.role: A hollow where water gathers supplies a catchment image for accumulated reports.
Consequential reports are the dispersed material gathered by the analogy.
The check or barrier is the pressure-like function produced by accumulation.
Water bursting from an outlet initiates the context's hydraulic accumulation.
Pouring and inpouring supply volume and sustained pressure.
Two flows meeting turns dispersed sources into one convergent force.

changed_reading.before: Individual reports arrive one after another with separate warnings.
changed_reading.after: As a contained material analogy, the reports form a catchment in which dispersed precedents converge until their restraining pressure becomes difficult to evade.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it activates the camel-specific z-j-r branch; it remains anchored through the focus noun and the context's sequence of seeing, turning away, and warnings not availing. Render it as an animal-behavior analogy for split reception, not as a claim that muzdajar denotes a camel.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: Muzdajar at 54:4 can carry an exploratory branch image in which recognition and yielding come apart.

activation_trace.role: The camel that recognizes by sight yet refuses and withholds supplies a model of divided reception.
Actual seeing supplies recognition on the perceptual side of the split.
Turning the side away supplies refusal after recognition.
Negated sufficiency marks the withheld benefit that recognition failed to release.

changed_reading.before: Failure to heed the reports implies failure to perceive their evidentiary force.
changed_reading.after: The audience may perceive the sign yet withhold assent and benefit; recognition and responsive yielding are separate events.

strongest_changes: The preceding reception sequence makes muzdajar an available but resistible brake rather than an automatic effect.
The exact z-j-r recurrence in 54:9 reverses the force: hearers rebuke the messenger who brings material meant to rebuke them.
The Noah sequence turns deterrence into an ordered causal precedent, not a bare threat.
The vessel, retained sign, recollection, and recitation form a durable transmission architecture for the reports.
summary.what_was_special: The same restraint root reverses social direction, while the surrounding sequence converts warning from transient speech into both a consequence model and a recoverable cross-media trace.
remaining_uncertainties: Whether the wisdom of 54:5 functionally glosses 54:4 or begins an independent evaluation.
Whether the passive z-j-r recurrence in 54:9 should revise muzdajar's direction or only exemplify hostile suppression.
The hydraulic and recognition-withholding readings are anchored analogies, not lexical renderings.

reader_a.activated_readings_md: 1. **Report is meant to operate as a brake.** `ج ي ء` B001 supplies arrival, `ن ب ء` B002 news brought and reported, and `ز ج ر` B001 checking, rebuking, or driving back by voice. The relative construction places restraining capacity inside what arrived from the reports. The packet gives news and restraint; I infer that historical report is effective only when its voiced content interrupts conduct. The ayah reads the coming narratives as behavioral machinery, not passive information.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: The later Noah, ʿĀd, Thamud, Lot, and Pharaoh sequences are the arriving reports this ayah announces, and each is followed by a memory-test. Their recurrence confirms that `مُزْدَجَرٌ` is a designed checking function embedded in narrative form.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **`ن ب ء / B002` (news brought and reported), sharpened by `B001` (coming from one place to another).** The reports grammatically "come" to the audience, and 54:9 begins the first embodied earlier community. News therefore plays the role of a transported past crossing into the present focus window. The packet supplies arrival language and the subsequent historical scene; I infer report-as-arrival -> collapses safe temporal distance. **Reading change:** `ٱلْأَنۢبَاء` are not inert information about others, but arrivals that place the hearer inside the same causal pattern.
2. **`ز ج ر / B001` (rebuking, checking, or driving by voice).** The branch is reinforced by the caller in 54:6-8 and by Noah being `ٱزْدُجِرَ` in 54:9. `مُزْدَجَر` functions as behavioral force: a report can check its audience now, while ignored checking later becomes a voice that drives bodies. The packet supplies the repeated vocal-driving root; I infer refused restraint -> eventual compelled motion. **Reading change:** the ayah offers a practical braking mechanism, not merely a frightening topic.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 54:6-9 sharpened the vocal mechanism: the caller drives bodies, and Noah is himself driven by rebuke, so the report's restraint can reverse from voluntary checking into compulsory movement.

identity_judgment.rationale: Yetkili kaynak ifadesi, birini sertçe engelleme ve vazgeçirme çekirdeğini; hayvanı sözlü bir çağrıyla sürme kullanımını; etkilenen kişinin geri durmasını ve bu eylemden doğan sesi birlikte gösterir. Ses, kovma ve hayvan sürme kullanımlarında açıkça kurucudur; ancak insana yöneltilen her engelleme anlatımında ayrıca belirtilmediği için dalın bütününü zorunlu olarak sesli saymak fazla geniş olur.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Dal, sert engelleme çekirdeği ile hayvanı sesle harekete geçiren özel kullanımı ayırır; kuş hareketinden anlam çıkarma bu dala girmez.

lexicalization_scope.note: Yalın engelleme ve azarlama anlamı, devenin sesle sürülmesine bağlı kullanım ve bu eylemden türeyen ses adı ayrı tutulur.

concept_map.definition: Bir kişiyi ya da canlıyı sert bir uyarıyla yapmakta olduğu şeyden alıkoyma, geri çevirme veya uzaklaştırma eylemidir. Hayvan söz konusu olduğunda aynı yöneltici ses onu yürütüp sürmeye yarayabilir; eylemin sonucu geri durma, türemiş bir kullanım ise bu amaçla çıkarılan sestir.

facets.statement: Bir kişiyi ya da canlıyı sertçe uyararak bir davranıştan alıkoyma veya geri çevirme.
Deve ve benzeri hayvanları sözlü bir çağrıyla ayağa kaldırma, yürütme veya sürme.
Uyarılan kişinin geri durması veya kötü bir davranıştan vazgeçmesi.
Engelleme ya da sürme amacıyla çıkarılan tek ve güçlü ses.
Gür ve uğultulu bir sesin, bu yöneltici ses eylemiyle kökensel olarak ilişkilendirilmesi.

identity_judgment.rationale: Yetkili kaynak ifadesi, deveye ilişkin iki bedensel niteliği tek dalda verir: omurlarında çökme bulunan veya sırtı yaralanmış deve ile sağrısındaki ağırlık yüzünden neredeyse kalkamayan dişi deve. Geçici çerçeve iki cinsiyete ve iki beden bölgesine bağlı ayrımı doğru biçimde korur.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Dal sırt ve sağrıdaki fiziksel kusurlarla sınırlıdır; yavruyu tanıma, kokudan yadırgama veya sütü esirgeme davranışı bu dala girmez.

lexicalization_scope.note: Sırt omurları çökmüş ya da yaralı deve niteliği ile sağrısı ağır olduğu için zor kalkan dişi deve tamlaması birbirine karıştırılmaz.

concept_map.definition: Devede sırt veya sağrı bölgesindeki belirgin bir bedensel kusuru bildiren niteliktir. Erkek deve kullanımında omurların çökmesi ya da sırt yarası, dişi deve kullanımında ise sağrının ağırlaşması ve bu yüzden hayvanın güçlükle ayağa kalkması öne çıkar.

facets.statement: Devenin sırt veya sağrı bölgesinde hareketini etkileyen bedensel kusur.
Erkek devenin sırt omurlarında çökme bulunması ya da sırtının yara içinde olması.
Dişi devenin sağrısındaki ağırlık yüzünden neredeyse ayağa kalkamaması.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kanıt, aynı adlandırma çevresinde iki ayrı deve kusurunu birlikte kaydeder: omur çökmesi veya sırt yarası ve sağrı ağırlığı yüzünden ayağa kalkma güçlüğü.
